Mission Local reported that SFMTA vice chair Gwyneth Borden was censured after being paid $12,500 by Fiorella to help legalize its outdoor deck. While serving on the transit board, she contacted planning staff, Planning Commission members and a supervisor seeking support for the restaurant. The story said the proposed fine was $9,000, though ethics commissioners were considering a higher penalty. Borden admitted breaking the rules and called it a mistake. She later resigned.

The first story also carries a correction: an earlier version incorrectly said Fiorella had the non-compliant deck before 2019; it belonged to Park Chow, which previously occupied the address.
